Subject: Calibration request: leveling & offer for James Lee (Infra)

Hi Neha / Monica —

Following yesterday's onsite, I want to flag a leveling disagreement before we send an offer. The interview panel strongly recommends James for a Senior/Staff-equivalent role given the scope he demonstrated; recruiting has him as L5. I outlined the core points below and attached the interview feedback and his resume.

Why I think L6 (summary):
- System design: led a deep-dive on distributed cache sharding that maps directly to a scaling gap we have; proposed a migration plan with measurable latency improvements.
- Ownership & impact: described owning a cross-team infra initiative at his last company that impacted 3 product lines and saved ~$1.2M/year.
- Mentorship/structure: has prior experience running postmortems and mentoring IC2+ engineers across orgs.

I realize HR is applying the rubric conservatively; I'm asking for a quick calibration call or an exception to propose an L6 offer (provisional review at 6 months) so we don't lose him. He's a strong fit for the infra team and the market is tight.

Attachments: resume_james_lee.pdf, candidate_feedback.pdf

Can we sync today? If HR maintains L5 I need the full rationale to share with the panel and the recruiter.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Hiring Manager, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Note: recruiter contact is Susan Park at Equation Talent (susan@equationtalent.com)

Subject: Re: Calibration request: leveling & offer for James Lee (Infra)

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the context and the write-up.

Quick summary of HR's position: based on our leveling rubric (impact, scope, org reach, and sustained ownership) the interview packet as submitted maps to L5. Specific notes the panel emphasized were strong design thinking and cross-team communication but limited evidence of sustained org-wide ownership at scale.

That said, I'm open to calibration. Two asks so we can move fast:
1) Please add 2–3 concrete, attributable examples (from the interview or his past work) that show sustained cross-org impact or a product-level ownership statement.
2) If you want an exception, propose the mitigation (e.g., 6-month review criteria / success metrics).

I'll book a 30-min calibration slot this afternoon. If we can align, we can approve a provisional L6 with explicit review criteria; if not, we should proceed with L5 and a stretch compensation package.

Neha Kapoor
Sr. Talent Partner, Redwood Inference

Neha —

Thanks for the fast reply. Below are the concrete examples you asked for (pulled from notes and the candidate):

1) Migration ownership: At his last employer (InfraCo), James led a phased migration of the global cache layer that he described as the single largest reliability project for their payments infra in 2023. He ran the design, led two teams, and owned the rollout plan. Post-migration metrics he shared: 40% reduction in cross-region cache miss rate and 18% lower end-to-end latency. This is not a short-lived project — it spanned 9 months and touched billing, search, and auth services.

2) Cross-team influence: He produced a quarterly SLO report that he owned and used to drive policy changes across product teams; engineering leads credited him with establishing the runbook used across three product teams.

3) Mentorship & process: He ran incident retros for the platform team and instituted on-call rotation changes that improved MTTR by ~22% per his metrics. He explicitly described hiring and mentoring junior engineers and setting career ladders.

Proposed mitigation if we provisionally promote to L6:
- Offer L6 title with a 6-month performance review focused on the migration project metrics (cache miss rate and latency targets) and cross-team adoption of his runbook.
- If metrics are not met, role will remain at L6 but compensation will be adjusted per standard HR practice (we can define exact success gates).

I can join the calibration call; if we agree, I'd like to authorize a market-competitive package now so recruiter doesn't lose momentum.

Karthik
Hiring Manager, Infrastructure
